scope: public excerpts and original synthesis; no product audit

records.title: Brand strategy and identity
records.definition: Define audience, problem, competitive alternatives, positioning, promise, personality and brand architecture; use research and brief before visual explorations. Separate brand voice, logo, typography, imagery, color and motion; build usage rules for product, marketing and print. Compare 2–3 directions against same brief, not arbitrary hue associations. Test recognition, differentiation and task performance; obtain owner approval.
records.limit: Method synthesis; no universal number of alternatives.

records.title: Color theory and harmony
records.definition: Hue, lightness/value, chroma and saturation are distinct; tint/shade/tone are traditional mixing concepts, not exact CSS operations. Explore monochromatic, analogous, complementary, split-complementary, triadic, tetradic and square harmonies as hypotheses. Wheel angles depend on chosen color model. Vary hierarchy and surface area; compare identical foreground colors on differing surrounds (simultaneous contrast).
records.limit: Educational methods, not accessibility guarantees or causal laws.

records.title: Color perception and psychology
records.definition: Color can influence affect, cognition and behavior; context, culture, task, prior learning and stimulus properties moderate effects. Do not claim blue always means trust or red always means danger. Test matched alternatives with representative users, neutral wording, counterbalanced order, controlled contrast and recorded uncertainty.
records.limit: Review abstract explicitly notes limits to generalization; no full-paper audit.

records.title: Color science and reproduction
records.definition: RGB is additive; CMYK device/print-dependent subtractive process. HSL/HSV are useful selection models, not perceptually uniform. CIE XYZ/Lab/LCH and Oklab/OKLCH describe color differently; OKLCH L is perceptual lightness, C chroma, H hue, not WCAG luminance. sRGB and Display P3 have different gamuts. Specify target space, white point/profile where relevant, gamut-map and verify output; for print use actual ICC profiles and proof, not universal RGB-to-CMYK conversion. CSS Color 4/5 maturity and browser support are separate.
records.limit: Draft specifications are not guarantees of browser behavior.

records.title: Color system engineering
records.definition: Choose seed, neutrals and distinct semantic families; derive ramps with target gamut, role contrast and usable chroma. Map primitive → semantic → component/state tokens; retain on-color pairs. Brand logo may differ from action accent. Material tonal palettes, Radix 12-step role scales and IBM 12 grades are distinct conventions, not interchangeable. Use semantic roles for surface/text/border/action/status/selection/focus/data; specify default/hover/pressed/disabled/selected/invalid and theme mappings. Check alpha against actual backdrop, gradients at worst case, and forced colors.
records.limit: No mandatory ramp count or 60/30/10 ratio.

records.title: Accessibility and evaluation
records.definition: WCAG 2.2 AA normal text 4.5:1; large text 3:1; applicable non-text cues 3:1 against adjacent colors. Evaluate exceptions and exact pairs without rounding up. Redundant labels/icons/patterns; test color-vision simulation, keyboard focus, forced colors, both themes, screenshots and assistive technology. Categorical/sequential/diverging encodings by data semantics. Contrast automation is necessary but not sufficient.
records.limit: APCA is not a WCAG 2.2 substitute; actual product audit still required.

records.title: Governance and handoff
records.definition: Record role, value, color space, allowed pairs, forbidden uses, theme overrides, contrast tests, owner and source. Review changes with versioned token diff, alias resolution, visual regression and migration plan; maintain brand guidelines separate from product tokens and cross-reference them. Tools: Adobe palette guidance for exploration; browser rendered fixtures and existing archive test suite for verification. Track unresolved issues and compare same tasks before/after.
records.limit: Proposed operational workflow; no claim that tests were run here.

records.title: Gestalt similarity, figure-ground and competing cues
records.definition: Similar hues can group objects; figure-ground and proximity can reinforce or compete. Apply consistent color to equivalent roles and combine labels/shape/spacing; test whether users identify the groups correctly.
records.limit: Perceptual grouping is context-sensitive, not an exclusive color law.

records.title: Preattentive features, selective attention and Guided Search 6.0
records.definition: Hue can guide visual search; top-down goals, bottom-up salience, history, reward and scene context influence priority. Compare time to find and error rates with matched distractors; avoid competing accent colors.
records.limit: Guidance is not a guarantee of instantaneous detection; Guided Search 6.0 is a newer model, not a normative standard.

records.title: Von Restorff isolation versus salience
records.definition: Distinctiveness can improve memory in isolation paradigms; visual salience and memory are separate outcomes. Use a distinct meaningful accent sparingly, measure detection and recall separately.
records.limit: Does not establish conversion or task success.

records.title: Simultaneous color contrast and chromatic adaptation
records.definition: Surround changes perceived color; temporal adaptation and contextual induction are distinct contributors. Compare the same token on actual surfaces, themes and ambient viewing conditions; validate separately from numerical WCAG contrast.
records.limit: Mechanisms and magnitude depend on conditions; do not infer a universal correction factor.

records.title: Stroop effect and semantic color interference
records.definition: Conflicting word meaning and ink color can interfere with a color-naming task. In product design, avoid conflicting learned status colors and labels; use consistent text, icon and color for success/error. Compare congruent and conflicting alternatives with identical task, contrast and content; measure response time, errors and comprehension.
records.limit: Experimental color-word effect is not proof of a universal red/green convention or a fixed UI performance penalty; localize and test. Color labels are a design extrapolation.

records.title: Opponent processing and color vision
records.definition: Trichromatic cone signals are processed by opponent neural mechanisms; historical red–green and blue–yellow appearance models are not identical to physiological channels. Distinguish opponent encoding from complementary wheel hues, and account for variation in color vision; pair status color with labels/icons and validate with representative users.
records.limit: Historical Hering/Hurvich–Jameson links between neural opponency and unique hue appearance are challenged; do not treat them as settled or use them as palette-generation rules.

records.title: Color constancy and viewing conditions
records.definition: Perceived surface color may remain relatively stable as illumination changes; constancy is imperfect and differs by scene, stimulus and observer. Distinguish it from chromatic adaptation, simultaneous contrast and display color management. For product QA compare identical tokens in actual themes and device/ambient conditions, with calibrated reference where fidelity matters.
records.limit: Reflective-surface laboratory results do not directly establish color behavior on emissive displays; no claim of guaranteed constancy.

records.title: CIECAM16, CAM16, CAT16 and CAM16-UCS
records.definition: CIE 248:2022 CIECAM16 supersedes CIECAM02 report CIE 159:2004; uses viewing-condition-dependent transforms of XYZ to appearance correlates and a chromatic adaptation transform. CAM16 is the underlying appearance model, CAT16 the adaptation transform, CAM16-UCS a derived approximately uniform space. Useful for calibrated cross-media appearance matching and color-difference research. Record white point, adapting luminance, background and surround; validate implementation against published reference values before use.
records.limit: Not a CSS-required space, mandatory design system algorithm or replacement for WCAG. Full CIE report not reviewed; do not implement equations from summary.

records.title: Color discrimination, MacAdam ellipses and Delta E
records.definition: MacAdam's psychophysical experiments show that chromaticity discrimination varies across the color diagram under specified viewing conditions. Delta E measures color difference in a stated model: distinguish Euclidean CIELAB ΔE76, CIEDE2000 ΔE00 (ISO/CIE 11664-6:2022), OKLab distance and CAM16-UCS distance. Use one documented metric for brand tolerance or token drift and compare actual rendered adjacent state colors; test recognition without hue alone.
records.limit: No universal ΔE=1 just-noticeable threshold or mandatory spacing between palette steps. ΔE is not WCAG contrast, and discriminability depends on area, context, observer, luminance and viewing conditions.

records.title: Feature Congestion, visual clutter and color competition
records.definition: Rosenholtz et al. compare Feature Congestion, Subband Entropy and Edge Density; color variability contributes to clutter in their experiments. Reserve accent for meaningful priorities; separate category/status/selection encoding; use neutral secondary surfaces and redundant labels. Compare matched task screens with varied color complexity, measure search time, errors and missed states; preserve information and avoid hiding essential cues.
records.limit: No universal maximum hue count, saturation threshold or guarantee of task performance. Feature Congestion is a research measure, not an accessibility criterion.
